sentence_stem: Had she been informed of the delay earlier,
correct_completion: she would have rearranged her entire schedule.
full_sentence: Had she been informed of the delay earlier, she would have rearranged her entire schedule.
acceptable_variants: she would have changed all her plans.
she would have adjusted her whole timetable.

options.text: she rearranges her schedule every day.
options.why_wrong: The present simple describes a habit and does not fit the hypothetical past condition set up by 'Had ... been informed'; the main clause needs 'would have' plus a past participle.

options.text: she will rearrange her schedule tomorrow.
options.why_wrong: A future form does not fit a third conditional, which requires 'would have' plus a past participle in the main clause.

options.text: she would have rearranged her entire schedule.
she had rearranged her schedule already.
options.why_wrong: The past perfect reports a completed past fact, not the hypothetical result that the inverted conditional requires.

explanation: The inverted 'Had' opening makes this a third conditional, so the main clause must use 'would have' with a past participle. Polish speakers may reach for a simple past or a future form here, because Polish builds its conditional with a separate particle rather than an auxiliary verb, so the English auxiliary pattern needs to be learned as a fixed structure.
